sentences.text: This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/ physical mode).
This is an application for bail.
Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the State.

The appellant-petitioner has been convicted for the offence under sections 363/366/376(2)(i)(l) of the Indian Penal Code read with section 6 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for a period of five years and to pay a fine of Rs.5,000/- (rupees five thousand), in default, to undergo further // 2 // R.I. for a period of three months for the offence under section 363 of the Indian Penal Code, to undergo R.I. for five years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- (rupees ten thousand), in default, to undergo further R.I. for four months for the offence under section 366 of the Indian Penal Code and to undergo R.I. for fourteen years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- (rupees ten thousand) in default to undergo further R.I. for six months for the offence under section 6 of the POCSO Act and no separate sentence has been imposed for the offence under section 376(2)(i)(l) of Suresh Purty vs State Of Odisha on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60340446/
1 the I.P.C. and all the sentences were directed to run concurrently by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge -cum -cum -Special Court under POCSO Act, Cuttack in Spl. G.R. Case No. 13 of 2015.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is in judicial custody since 04.03.2015 and the victim being examined as P.W.7 was held to be a mentally retarded person and thereafter she was declared hostile and leading questions have been put by the learned Special Public Prosecutor to the victim and though the victim admitted during questions put that the petitioner committed rape on her for three times inside the jungle but in the cross-examination, she stated that // 3 // she had gone to the jungle for collecting Kendu leaves and the petitioner found her alone inside the jungle, brought her to the village and on that date, for the first time, she talked with the petitioner.

entities.text: Suresh Purty vs State Of Odisha
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner further submitted that the medical evidence adduced by P.W.4 indicates that there was no bodily injury detected on the person of the victim and there was no sign of recent sexual intercourse.

It is further submitted that there is a good chances of success in the appeal and balance of convenience in his favour and in view of the period of detention in judicial custody, the bail application of the petitioner may be favourably considered.
Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail ant and placed the evidence of P.W.4 and P.W.7.

Considering the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner, nature of evidence adduced by the prosecution during trial, absence of any chance of early hearing of the appeal in the near future and balance of convenience being in his favour and further taking into account the period of detention of the petitioner in judicial custody, I am inclined to release the petitioner on bail.
// 4 // Let the appellant-petitioner be released on bail pending disposal of the appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court on such other conditions as the learned trial Court may deem just and proper The I.A. is accordingly disposed of.

There shall be stay of realization of fine amount imposed by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge -cum- Special Court under POCSO Act, Cuttack in Spl. G.R. Case No. 13 of 2015 till disposal of the criminal appeal.
Issue certified copy as per rules.
